content: China has confirmed that President Xi Jinping will host US President Donald Trump and Russian President Vladimir Putin for a trilateral summit in Shenzhen on Thursday, November 19. It will be the first time the leaders of the world's three largest military powers have met together in this format. The Chinese Foreign Ministry announced the meeting in a brief statement on Monday, saying Xi will hold a China-Russia-US heads of state meeting with Putin and Trump in Shenzhen. Beijing did not publish a detailed agenda for the talks. The White House had already signalled the meeting was coming. A White House spokeswoman said on Friday that Trump will hold a joint meeting with Putin and Xi during a summit in China this week. The confirmation from Beijing makes the date and the venue official: Thursday, November 19, in the southern tech hub of Shenzhen. The choice of Shenzhen is itself notable. The city is China's leading technology and manufacturing centre, and it has rarely hosted a summit of this scale. Holding the meeting there, rather than in Beijing, puts China's economic transformation at the centre of the imagery of the event. The summit comes at a moment of acute tension. The war between the United States and Iran has escalated sharply in recent days, with Iran claiming a drone attack on the US-allied Gulf state of Bahrain on Sunday, and Washington sending a third aircraft carrier, the USS Roosevelt, to the Middle East. Tankers have also been struck in the Strait of Hormuz, the waterway through which a large share of the world's oil is shipped. The war in Ukraine continues as well. Kyiv launched its biggest overnight drone attack on Russia since the war began, according to Ukrainian Defence Ministry data released on Monday, and nuclear safety regulators have warned that the risk of a nuclear accident in Ukraine is increasing this winter. Against that backdrop, a meeting of the three leaders carries weight beyond the usual diplomacy. The United States, China and Russia are the three permanent members of the UN Security Council with the largest nuclear arsenals, and their relations have been strained for years over trade, technology, Taiwan, Ukraine and the Middle East. A joint meeting does not by itself resolve any of those disputes, but it creates a channel at the highest level at a time when several conflicts are running in parallel. No joint statement or expected outcome has been announced. The three sides have each said little beyond confirming the meeting, and it is not yet clear whether the talks will produce agreements or serve mainly as a signal that the leaders are talking. What is certain is the symbolism. Three leaders who have spent much of the past decade in confrontation will sit at the same table on Thursday, in a Chinese city built on global trade, while wars rage in the Middle East and Europe. The world will be watching what, if anything, comes out of the room.
summary: Beijing has confirmed that China's Xi Jinping will meet US President Donald Trump and Russian President Vladimir Putin in Shenzhen on Thursday, in the first three-way summit of the three leaders.
title: Xi to host Trump and Putin in Shenzhen on November 19 for first trilateral summit
